chapter_title: [Concerning the Five] Greatnesses who [went forth] against the Darkness.
chapter_note: Dominantly CORE: a systematic pentadic listing of the five Greatnesses (emanational series) followed by a long, internally-cosmic exposition of the five ‘advents’ via similes (judge, king inspecting works, butter in milk) and eschatological mechanics (Summons/Obedience; Last Statue; great fire). Later layers appear as (a) FRAME dialogue-attribution at the start, (b) a few small audience-address intrusions (MIXED), (c) a Christian salvation-history/tree-of-life segment tied to Adam/Eve (OVERLAY), and (d) a closing beatitude/exhortation (PASTORAL).

paragraphs.core_text: [...] the Darkness, it was defeated by five greatnesses.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic dialogue frame attribution: “Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples:” and the opening quotation punctuation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching claim is cosmological and impersonal; the speaker-attribution to ‘the enlightener’ is a later Kephalaia frame wrapper.

paragraphs.core_text: The first greatness is the Father of Greatness who exists in calm and hiddenness; as he is established in his light-earth, in his own essence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal cosmological definition (being→state/place/essence), no citation, no audience address.

paragraphs.core_text: Four greatnesses were manifested and came forth of him. They were appointed to ten parts, and established in total twelve.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumerative degree/number structure (pentad, ten, twelve) characteristic of the systematic teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The second greatness poured out and was manifested. It was revealed from the first greatness. It is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, together with the First Man and his five sons; these are the second greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanational chain stated as ontology (“revealed from”), with fixed cosmic names and a fivefold sub-structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The third greatness is the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder, the Living Spirit, and the five sons of the Living Spirit. These are the third greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cataloguing of cosmic hypostases and their pentadic entourage; page marker removed per rules.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth greatness is the Third Ambassador, and the Pillar of Glory, and all the light powers who were revealed from him. These are the fourth greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the impersonal emanational schema; cosmos→cosmos mapping only.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth greatness who came from the Father is Jesus the Splendour, and all his powers whom he summoned, his emanations who were [...] They poured out and were manifested from him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Though ‘Jesus’ vocabulary triggers a Christian register, this paragraph functions purely as a cosmological hypostasis within the emanational pentad, without Gospel citation or salvation-history narrative.

paragraphs.core_text: This is, so that they were spread out and [...] fives: these five [sons] of the First Man [...] the entire building; another five are the five sons of the Living Spirit who are spread out to five places, supporting [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit pentadic correspondential structuring (five→five→five places), purely internal to the cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] total in twelve parts that [... There are] another two added to them who are the summons and the obedience. They are the father and the mother whom Jesus the Splendour by his advent has appointed as successors to his place [...] the great earth and the [...] in them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numerical/theological rationalization stays within the system (cosmic entities, roles, places); no institutional or contemporary-world mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: [The advent ...] of the First Man who came [...] belonging to [...] existing in a kingdom [...] esteem before they who belong to his household [...] his enemies [...] and suffering by their wickedness; and they take from him [...] and a richness; and they imprison [him in] captivity and take from him their companies (?). Yet, he [...] by his humility; and he takes heart and restrains his enemy [...] in silence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pedagogical simile/narrativized exposition used to explain a cosmic event; still descriptive, not exhortative, and not anchored to contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as with this man, this noble son whose enemies surround him, this also is how the advent of the First Man happened, [...] rulers, the enemies of the light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicitly ties the simile back to cosmic rulers; internal mythic-historical explanation.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, the advent of the Living Spirit and the commandment that he received, whereby he came upon all the rulers, it differs from that of the First Man. His advent [...] the advent of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Comparative structural teaching of successive divine missions (‘advents’), not pastoral instruction.

paragraphs.core_text: The advent of the Living Spirit is like this, when he was sent from the greatness that he might bring up the First Man. He resembles a judge the king would send to overturn the violence to that man, the noble son against whom his enemies sinned. And he, this judge, [...] hard and cruel [...] and he gives the means [...] by his righteousness and his strength; and he also judges all who are condemned according to their rebellious heart, and repays each according to his deserts. They who are worthy of blows he strikes with hard leather whips. Again, these who are worthy of cutting off their limbs, or indeed their [...] and he repays them accordingly. [...] and he binds and fetters them, and hangs by [...] and thus he does to them with a righteous judgement. And he kills them to flay their skin [...] so that they will be killed by a death [...] until they die. Again, [they for] whom it is fitting [...] to banish from their dwellings he may remove according to a righteous judgement; just as they had faulted and sinned against the noble son.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extended correspondential simile (judge/king) explaining cosmic justice mechanics; no citation formulas or ecclesial targeting.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the associates in the mystery and the assistants of this judge, these who belong to him in great strength; in an instant and haste they shall do the will of their master.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still within the simile’s cosmic-judicial register; not institutional ‘mystery’ practice but assistants of the cosmic agent in the analogy.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, just as this genuine judge, who was sent from the king to overturn the violence to this man, the noble son: this is also the case with the Living Spirit. He also was sent from the King of the lights to overturn the vengeance and violence to the First Man, against whom the King of the realms of Darkness had sinned. He faulted and sinned against him, and also his rebellious powers. Therefore, when (the Living Spirit) came, he bore up the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear cosmos→cosmos mapping: King of Lights/Living Spirit/First Man vs. King of Darkness and powers; explanatory, not hortatory.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, all the rulers, the powers of Sin who had faulted and sinned against the sons of the First Man, he has judged them according to a righteous judgement. He has bound them in heaven and earth. He put each one to the place fitting for him; he weighed each of them according to his cruelty and oppression. While some of them he enclosed in the prison, others he hung head down. Some [...] are crucified, others are sat down all the time. Some among them are fixed beneath their associates, restricted by a strong chain; others he made the holders of authority over their companions beneath, so that they may do their pleasure amongst these below them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic punitive ordering of rulers across heaven/earth; ‘Sin’ functions as a cosmic power-category (personified force) within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: when the Father of Life established the judgements [...] He was revealed to all the powers of Darkness. He judged them as a true giver of judgement [...] This is the first judgement that the Living Spirit gave the rulers [in respect of the] First Man. Indeed, he gave victory to the First Man corresponding to his victory; but he condemned the King of the realms of Darkness corresponding to that by which he had erred.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed brief audience-address/bridging formula: “Happen you know this [...] that”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core content is a correspondential balancing of judgements/victory/condemnation within the cosmic system; the opening direct address is a later rhetorical intrusion.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] this chain, of this sort, became [...] the earth till the end time when the universe will be dissolved; and it perishes in the great fire and is separated. While the light goes to its country, the Darkness remains in the chain and fetter for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological mechanics (end time, dissolution, great fire, separation of light/Darkness) presented as process, not exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The advent also of the Third Ambassador, when he came to inspect they who are imprisoned in the zone: he is like a great king who comes and inspects craftsmen [...] and [...] and [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Advent + simile framed to explain a cosmic inspection in the ‘zone’; remains system-internal.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, they who are good, of the craftsmen and architects and artisans whom he has there in each place: he shall see that they have worked well, and have fallen to his works in their fashion. He shall rejoice with great joy [...] He shall thank the artisans who have constructed his works [and completed] his orders.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the king/inspection simile; pedagogical but not applied to church offices or ethics.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, just as this great king who comes and inspects his works and fortifications, so also is the advent of the Third Ambassador. For, when he too came, he saw [his works] established and prepared and [...] series of the rulers prepared and established there, above and below, outside and within, in the great pattern that his brothers had made. They had come before him to the contest, they who had fixed and created the universe before he came. He saw the gods and the angels established and controlling the fortifications [...] guarding the entire ruling-power [...] which his first powers had done. They are the First Man and the Living Spirit and the Great Spirit, the Mother of Life.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic architecture vocabulary (fortifications, pattern, rulers, gods/angels) with explicit internal identification of earlier powers.

paragraphs.core_text: Therefore, when he saw them, that they had created everything with great wisdom, [...] as they looked he plundered (?) [...] in his advent, by which he came, he was unveiled to them. He says to the Living Spirit: “The judgement that you have [...] good, what you uttered [...] you gave to them correspondingly; so that they were moved and raised up to that of which they were not worthy”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still intra-cosmic discourse (Third Ambassador addressing Living Spirit) evaluating judgement as a cosmic operation (‘correspondingly’), not citing Gospel/NT.

Tree/fig-garden destruction imagery in a ‘Jesus the Splendour’ advent context reads as Christianized salvation imagery and parable-like language; not a closed cosmos→cosmos mapping and plausibly mediated by Christian tradition.
‘tree of life’ planting and ‘good fruit’ language aligns with biblical/Christian symbolic stock; functions as salvation-history imagery rather than systematic cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this is like this simile of the advent of Jesus the Splendour. It happened like this; because he too set out [...] his power and his wisdom, in his [...]-ness [...] in his glorious wisdom he destroyed them. He bound and crushed them like the fire that shall burn and destroy trees. This is also how he performed his will in the zone, among the many powers,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the salvation-history pivot that reaches outside the cosmic system into biblical human narrative: “until he reached the form of the flesh of Adam and Eve, the first humans. [He perfected] his will in Eve, he [...] He also gave hope to Adam, and the good news [...] glorious [...] He went up to the heights [...] of light.” Also removed the immediately preceding phrase “a king and a saviour” as a likely Christianizing gloss embedded in a lacunose clause.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening portion is still cosmos-internal (Jesus the Splendour acting ‘in the zone’ among powers) and can stand alone; the Adam/Eve ‘good news’ section is a clear crossing into salvation-history narrative typical of later Christian overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: Then the summons and the obedience, the great counsel that came to the elements, which are set in conjunction: it mixed with them, it was established in silence. It bears up [...] until the end time when it can arise and stand firm in the great fire. It will gather to it its own soul, and sculpt it in the Last Statue. You will also find it sweeps out and casts from it the pollution that is foreign to it. However, the life and the light that are in all things it gathers in to it, and builds upon its body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly diagnostic core mechanics: cosmic mixture into elements, silent working, eschatological gathering, Last Statue formation—system process language.

paragraphs.core_text: The time when this Last Statue will be perfect in all its limbs, then it can become free and ascend from that great struggle through the Living Spirit its father, the one who comes and brings a [...] limb. He brings it up from within this gathering (?), the melting down and destruction of all things.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of eschatological process (perfection of limbs, ascent, destruction/melting); slight second-person residue is absent here—still descriptive.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, this counsel, that summons and obedience, resembles thus cooled butter. If a person will take and set it in hot milk, it melts down and soaks in with this hot milk. It melts in another time in silence and quiet to the midst [...] yet also, of the power and the taste of this milk [...] is drawn to (the butter), and (the milk) sets and becomes cold [...] in [...] and the [...] this milk it shall clarify and discard. However, the oil and the grease and the ‘beauty’ of the milk it shall gather in to it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic correspondential simile used to explain cosmic mixture/separation: sensory/physical process mapped onto metaphysical gathering and purification.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this too is what the advent of that thought is like, the counsel of life, which is the summons and obedience that came to the elements. This is the one that at the end can arise and stand firm, and will gather in to it all the lives, and the light that has remained behind in everything. It can build them upon its body; it will gather them in to it [...] in its image for ever and ever [...] from this time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative restatement of the ‘counsel’ as a cosmic collector/building-body principle; entirely system-internal eschatology.
Beatitude-style exhortation (‘Blessed is every one who will believe…’) addresses hearers’ belief and salvation; shifts from cosmological mechanism to audience-directed soteriological encouragement.
